small_guidance:
- The current kernel forces `BLOCK_M = next_pow2(OC) = 64` and loops the K dimension with `tl.static_range`, but tiles the spatial dim only. With OH*OW = 126*126 = 15876 per (N), and N=128, you have ~128 programs × ~62 spatial tiles at BLOCK_N=256. Try adding configs with `BLOCK_M=32` and tile OC as well (split program over OC tiles) — currently every program redoes all 64 OC rows even when register pressure could be relieved by halving M and doubling spatial throughput.
- Add larger `BLOCK_K` configs (32, 48) to the autotune. With K_FLAT = 8·3·3 = 72, BLOCK_K=16 means ~5 static iterations with masked tail; BLOCK_K=72 (or 96 padded) processes the entire reduction in one `tl.dot`, eliminating the loop and the per-iter mask compute.
- Switch x to `channels_last` (NHWC) layout before the kernel so the IC axis (the GEMM-K) is contiguous in memory; the current NCHW gather along `ic_k * IH*IW` strides badly across the K loop. Pair with autotune configs at `num_warps=8, num_stages=3`.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as an implicit-GEMM conv in NHWC: pack input as (N, IH, IW, IC) and weight as (OC, KH, KW, IC) (or (KH·KW·IC, OC)), then tile over (N·OH·OW) as the M dimension and OC as the N dimension. K = KH·KW·IC = 72 fits in a single tile, so the kernel becomes one `tl.dot` per program with no K loop — drastically reducing index math overhead. This is the standard high-performance conv shape for small kernels.
- One program per `(M_tile of N·OH·OW, OC_tile)` with `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=72` (padded to 128). Total programs ≈ (128·126·126/128) × (64/64) ≈ 15876 — far more parallelism than the current (128, ~62) = 7936 grid. Fuse the BN+scale epilogue (already folded into per-OC scale/bias) directly before the store.
- Avoid the OC zero-padding hack (OC=64 is already pow2 here, but in general): make BLOCK_N a tunable that masks the OC tail rather than allocating padded weight tensors at every forward call — that allocation alone is measurable overhead at this kernel's runtime scale.
